acceptance.given: The Toolchain has an Exact Cover graph containing behavioral-duty obligation nodes and their assertion, selector, command, witness, and runtime-evidence bindings.

oracle.expected: Exact Cover validation verifies that every behavioral-duty obligation has its own observable fault witness and independently attributable runtime observation; a witness or observation bound for one behavioral duty cannot alone prove another behavioral duty.
forbidden: A behavioral-duty obligation has no observable independent fault witness.
A fault witness or its sole runtime observation is treated as proof for a different behavioral duty without an independent observation.
oracle.observable: The compiled Exact Cover validation result includes per-behavioral-duty witness and runtime-evidence bindings, and rejects a graph with a missing or shared-only behavioral fault witness.

acceptance.then: The semantic result rejects incomplete behavioral-duty fault-witness coverage.
acceptance.when: Quick Dev executes the Exact Cover validation selector against a graph containing behavioral-duty witness bindings.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate one behavioral-duty binding to reuse the sole fault witness and runtime observation of another behavioral duty; the executable Exact Cover selector must reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The Toolchain compiler entry rejects Exact Cover output when a behavioral duty lacks its own observable independent fault witness or relies solely on another behavioral duty's witness observation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing lifecycle, terminal-category, and non-authorizing semantics; only invalid Exact Cover witness bindings become rejecting outcomes.

slice_hint.state_transition: A graph with a missing or shared-only behavioral-duty fault witness transitions from an otherwise coverable graph to a rejected semantic result; independently observed per-duty witnesses remain valid.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector passes only if every behavioral-duty node has an independently observable fault witness and attributable runtime observation; a missing or shared-only witness causes rejection.
